name: Warrior Pose
intro:
Warrior Pose (Virabhadrasana I) is a powerful standing yoga posture that builds strength, stability, and confidence. Inspired by the stance of a warrior, this pose engages the entire body while promoting focus and determination. It involves a deep lunge with arms raised overhead, creating a strong connection between the lower and upper body.

This pose strengthens the legs, shoulders, and core while improving balance and coordination. It also stretches the chest, lungs, and hips, helping to open up the body and improve breathing capacity. The grounded stance combined with upward reach encourages both physical strength and mental clarity.

Regular practice of Warrior Pose enhances endurance and posture while reducing stiffness in the lower body. It is especially beneficial for building stamina and increasing body awareness. The pose also promotes confidence and inner strength, making it a key posture in many yoga sequences.

steps.text: Start by standing straight in Mountain Pose (Tadasana).
Step one foot back, keeping the front knee bent at 90 degrees.
Turn the back foot slightly outward and press it firmly into the ground.
Raise your arms overhead with palms facing each other.
Keep your torso upright and look forward or slightly upward.
Hold the pose while maintaining steady breathing.

benefits: Strengthens legs, arms, shoulders, and core muscles
Enhances flexibility of hips, chest, and lungs
Encourages deep breathing and lung expansion
Increases focus, confidence, and mental strength
Helps reduce stiffness in the lower body
Supports better circulation throughout the body
Builds overall physical and mental resilience
avoid: You have high blood pressure (avoid raising arms for long)
You have knee or ankle injuries
You suffer from shoulder pain or injury
You feel dizziness or imbalance while holding the pose
You are recovering from recent surgery
You experience pain while performing the pose
